Ward.player_timing: before player mana refill and normal draw
Ward.enemy_timing: enemy action start, after all damage-over-time ticks, including skipped actions

damage_over_time.timing: player turn end, after unkept cards are discarded
damage_over_time.application: maximum of existing and incoming value, separately per status

Scry.scope: current top of library, follows changes

Keep.source: return marked source after resolution, within hand cap
Keep.marker_loss: leaving hand or after end-turn discard

Flip.self: resolving physical source; finish original played description
Flip.top_of_pile: visible named top card, no choice
Flip.random: automatic, uniformly without replacement after payment

Ward.definition: Absorb incoming damage before HP. At the start of its holder’s turn, halve remaining Ward, rounding down. Remove it at 0.
notes: Player Ward halves before mana refill and draw. Enemy Ward halves when its action begins, after damage-over-time ticks, even if Hush skips the action.
New Ward adds to remaining Ward. Ward absorbs direct damage, Burn and Poison, but does not stop separate status or card-movement effects. No effect tests whether damage reached Ward or HP.

Burn.definition: At player turn end, deal Fire damage equal to Burn, then halve Burn, rounding down. Remove it at 0. Applying Burn keeps the higher value; it does not add.
notes: Resolve player Burn, player Poison, enemy Burn, then enemy Poison. Stop if a combatant is defeated.
Ward absorbs the tick. Mark, weakness, Weaken, Reflect and Leech do not modify it. An enemy applies Burn after the tick step; it first ticks at the following player turn end.

Poison.definition: At player turn end, deal Decay damage equal to Poison, then halve Poison, rounding down. Remove it at 0. Applying Poison keeps the higher value; it does not add.
notes: Poison and Burn are separate counters and can coexist. Neither application replaces the other.
Use the same timing and damage rules as Burn, including Ward absorption. Poison represents venom, toxic contamination or lingering sickness where the artwork supports it.

Scry.definition: Reveal the top card of your library for the rest of this player turn. If the top changes, reveal the new top.
notes: Scry has no choice, discard, movement or reshuffle. An empty library shows no card; reveal its top if another effect refills it before the turn ends.
Repeated Scry does not stack. Clear it when End Turn begins, before discarding cards. The library is the draw pile.

Mark.definition: Add Mark to the next direct attack against its holder, before Ward, then remove Mark. Mark adds together and affects only the first hit.
notes: The player normally Marks the enemy; an enemy effect explicitly names the player when it Marks them.
Mark does not affect Burn, Poison or separate trait damage.

Weaken.definition: Reduce the holder’s next direct attack by Weaken, to a minimum of 0, then remove Weaken. Weaken adds together and affects only the first hit.
notes: Weaken persists through non-attack actions.
A player effect says “Weaken 4”; an enemy effect explicitly applies Weaken to the player.

Hush.definition: Suppress the enemy’s labeled trait through its next action. Skip a non-attack ability; an attack keeps its base hits. Advance the pattern normally.
notes: Hush starts immediately and ends after the action’s aftereffects, including traits active while the intent is shown.
Hush does not undo existing Ward, damage, revealed cards, or an already-applied next-turn effect. Ward still halves at the enemy action start.
Hush does not stack. A pure Hush card needs a suppressible ability or trait in the current intent. A conditional trait counts even before its condition is met.
Every current Hush face Banishes its source.

Keep.definition: Mark the stated cards to survive this turn’s discard on their current faces. “Keep this card” returns the resolving source to your hand, marked, when its effect finishes.
notes: “Keep your hand” marks the cards currently in hand and excludes the resolving source. Random targets are picked automatically without replacement; use all available cards if fewer exist.

Kept cards remain playable and count toward the 8-card cap. A source returning through Keep also obeys the cap; if no slot remains, discard it instead. Every current self-Keep effect leaves room for its source.
A card leaving the hand loses its marker. Kept cards lose their markers after the end-turn discard. Next turn draw up to 5 new cards within the 8-card cap.
Enemy held-card effects check the actual hand after discard. There is no retained-card snapshot or prior identity tracking.

Flip.definition: Turn the stated cards to their other faces. Whole-hand, self, top-of-pile and random targets are explicit and require no selection prompt.
notes: “Flip your hand” changes only the current hand and excludes the resolving source. “Flip this card” changes the resolving physical source; finish the effect printed on the face that was played.

Pick random cards after paying, uniformly without replacement. If fewer exist, use all available cards. Show the eligible pool before play and the result afterward; do not reveal or reroll a hidden outcome on hover or cancellation.
Cards keep their faces through movement and reshuffling. A flipped source normally enters the discard pile on its new face; self-Keep instead returns it to hand on that face.

Banish.definition: Remove the physical card, including both faces, for this fight. Return it to the run deck afterward. Banished cards cannot be recovered during a fight.
notes: This spends the depicted opportunity for the encounter; it need not mean that a depicted creature literally dies.
An enemy’s Banish can remove a player card; show its destination and that it returns after the fight.

Reflect.definition: Redirect the next attack’s first hit to its attacker, keeping its final damage and type. Then Reflect ends. Reflect does not stack.
notes: Apply Mark, weakness and Weaken before reflection; do not apply them again at the new target. The attacker’s Ward can absorb the returned hit unless the hit ignores Ward.
A reflected hit cannot be reflected again. A 0-damage hit still spends Reflect. Burn, Poison and separate trait damage are not attacks.
A trait may specify an earlier expiry, such as the end of its displayed intent. Hush suspends that trait’s reflection immediately.

Leech.definition: Heal for the attack’s final damage after bonuses and Weaken, before Ward. Count Ward absorption and overkill. Healing stops at maximum HP.
notes: For multiple hits with Leech, total their final damage values; do not track HP actually lost.
Leech is healing attached to that attack, not a damage type or a second hidden effect. It cannot revive an attacker already defeated.
Food, medicine and other fixed heals remain fixed heals.

weakness_frequency: once per direct attack card, first hit
ordinary_instructions: Draw, heal, look, shuffle, exchange, turn and zone movements are stated in full; they are not separate thematic tags.
